intro.description: This cheat sheet guides you through the Platform Status Cleanup. The cleanup removes only status codes that are provably equivalent to IStatus.OK and retains severity, explicit plug-in identity, message, and throwable.

item.title: Understand the Safe Transformation
item.description:
A supported five-argument constructor can use the shorter constructor that assumes an OK code:
Before
new Status(IStatus.ERROR, Activator.PLUGIN_ID, IStatus.OK, message, exception)
After
new Status(IStatus.ERROR, Activator.PLUGIN_ID, message, exception)
The plug-in identity remains explicit. The cleanup does not replace the call with Status.error(...) because that factory infers identity from the calling bundle and may produce a different IStatus.getPlugin() value.

item.title: Enable the Cleanup
item.description:
Open the Clean Up dialog to enable the Platform Status cleanup:
1. In the Package Explorer, select an Eclipse plug-in project
2. Choose Source → Clean Up…
3. Select Use custom profile and click Configure…
4. On the Platform Status (Sandbox) tab, enable the cleanup
5. Click OK
Click Perform to open the Source menu.

item.title: Review the Real Execution Preview
Understand MultiStatus Handling
item.description:
MultiStatus may carry an application-specific code. The cleanup changes only a value that is provably zero:
new MultiStatus(pluginId, 0, message, exception)
→ new MultiStatus(pluginId, IStatus.OK, message, exception)
A nonzero constant, method call, or unresolved expression is deliberately left unchanged.
